title: White and black pay gaps
summary: Booking agents pay white musicians more and black musicians accept it; he refuses to play for less than white players get.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Of the musicians that were around, the ones who were talking, well, this guy's trying to cut my throat, did any of the black musicians ever talk about a situation of the white musicians -

Yeah, getting more work. The fact that there were a lot of white men involved in the music industry, like John Hammond - were there any black people involved that you recall that were able to get work for musicians and recordings for musicians?

Well, so far as John is concerned, I don't know, John isn't so prejudiced, but there are booking agents who pay white musicians much more than they would the Negro musicians and the Negroes would accept it. I've had people offer me jobs and I'd say, 'Huh-uh ... you pay me what you pay him and I'll play for you.' Of course if one will do it, another one will do it. As long as you keep yourself down, you're going to stay down.

When the musicians got together to talk about those bad things that were happening to their lives, what kind of things did you hear them say? I mean, would one musician talk about how so-and-so gypped him, how he made this record for this guy and didn't get paid. Did you hear stuff like that?
Sometimes you would hear remarks about different things like that. When I got out I didn't like to talk about music.
No, I don't want to hear nothing about it.
